one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event in the window: Q3 2026 results Tue 2026-11-10 before the open (guide net sales 36-37M, non-GAAP EPS -0.20 to -0.12 [5]). Base rate from its own 4 prints: revenue beat the guide midpoint 4/4 (median +8.4%) and EPS beat the top of the range 4/4 [notes, 1-5,12]; the May print moved the stock +45% in a day [25], so the event adds a fat tail. Against that: the beat record is known and priced, the guide flags supply constraints [5], and the stock is in a downtrend (90.48 June close to 43.31, -18% in October [15]) with a semis breadth backdrop that has shown extreme drops this year [30]; short-horizon momentum points down. Net: median 43.6 (slight tilt up for a probable beat), lognormal spread 0.25 for the month (annual vol 82%/3.5 = 0.23, widened a little for the print).

reasoning: Base-rates lane. Anchors: (1) small-company IPOs underperform style-matched firms by 17% over 3 years and the market by 36% (Gao-Ritter-Zhu, 1980-2009 [22]); AMBQ is 15 months past a July-2025 IPO at $24, so the base rate leans against the median drifting up; lockup expiries are a small, known effect (-1.5% 3-day [26]). (2) The stock's own history is the widest base rate: 25.39 in March 2026 to 90.48 in June and back to 43.31 [15], i.e. its own NTM sales multiple has spanned about 3.5x to well over 10x in 2026; 1-year realized vol 82%. (3) Macro event odds: Kalshi 2027 recession 20% [24]; moratorium appraisal near zero (-0.33/sh) [28]. Model: I keep the thread's quarterly driver set (drivers us_rev, cn_rev, row_rev, ng_gm, ng_opex) unchanged: revenue FY27 178.3 is within 0.1% of StockAnalysis consensus 178.4 [10], the Q3 beat set below the record's median is reasonable, and I see no base-rate evidence to move a driver. My views by driver: us_rev path fine but carries the concentration tail (downside -15%); cn_rev -40% downside for tariffs; row_rev +80% FY27 is the most optimistic (alternative +40% costs ~3% revenue); ng_gm path fine; ng_opex +22% FY27 is conservative vs management's 2028 profitability target [25] but consistent with the Q3 guide step [5] and IPO base rates [22]. Value carried by one EV/NTM-sales leg (the loss flag rules out P/E, EV/EBITDA, FCF yield): peer median 6.40x from 4 numeric good peers, own 4.87x, k = 0.8 gives 5.14x, base $47.96 (+11% vs 43.31). Scenarios move drivers and the multiple: P10 $22.08 (drivers down + multiple about 2.0x), P90 $90.61 (drivers up + multiple about 9.6x); log spreads 0.61 down and 0.50 up, below realized vol because part of 2026's swing was IPO-float and AI-sentiment specific. Source mix: 30 sources, 8 in lane; the 16 inherited from the thread set are filings and consensus pages for reported facts, which the brief allows; research was limited to about 14 searches/fetches. Not driver-linked: the moratorium adjustment (fixed -7.9 from the appraisal).

model_inputs.ebit_basis_note: EBIT = company non-GAAP gross profit - non-GAAP operating expense - D&A = GAAP loss from operations + SBC + severance + IPO-related bonus and transaction costs - the 2025 non-monetary gain (Ex.99.1 reconciliations). Q2 2026: -8.727 + 3.557 = -5.170 = 15.989 - 19.374 - 1.785 [5]. The company's own non-GAAP figures exclude D&A as well as SBC, so its "non-GAAP operating loss" (GP - opex) is EBITDA-like; this set deducts D&A to keep EBIT an EBIT (engine ebitda = ebit + da = the company figure). EPS in notes = company non-GAAP net loss per share (excl. SBC and D&A, incl. other income) on weighted basic shares, the basis of the guide and Street (StockAnalysis/Benzinga). Engine model EPS = EBIT / diluted shares (no other income) and is lower; Zacks figures are on a different, GAAP-like basis.

quarters.note: FY = calendar year. Actual = FY2025 (10-K [8]) + Q1 2026 (10-Q, release [4]) + Q2 2026 (10-Q [6], release [5]). downside.story: P10: a top-3 wearable customer (78% of Q2 2026 net sales [6]; no binding purchase commitments [8]) moves a program, China-HQ customers hit by tariffs or export controls, design wins slip, GM -2 pt; and the multiple de-rates to about 2.7x NTM sales, below SYNA (3.87x) and near AMBQ's own March-2026 trough, as small post-IPO names usually do in a semis down-leg (small-IPO 3-year style-adjusted -17% [22]; Kalshi 2027 recession 20% [24]); moratorium low case -1.34/sh [28].

upside.story: P90: supply constraints ease, edge-AI content keeps rising at the top customers, Atomiq/Apollo5 wins outside wearables convert, GM +1.5 pt, and the market pays about 8.1x NTM sales again (between AMBA/CEVA and LSCC; AMBQ itself traded far above that at the June 2026 high [15]); moratorium high case +0.82/sh [28].

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 2026 29.2 (+10.6% q/q, +80.6% y/y), Q4 31.8: the Q3 guide (36-37 total, "partially constrained by industry-wide supply availability" [5]) plus the record beat (4/4 above the midpoint, +2.3 to +16.6% [2-5]) shaded to +4% for the stated supply limit; CEO "on pace to more than double net sales in the second half of 2026" vs H2 2025 38.9 [5] -> H2 total 79.5 (2.04x). Growth is the new major customer product launch and upgrades to Apollo5/510 (10-Q: ASP up on customers moving to new products [6]). FY27 +25%, FY28 +18%, FY29 +14%: the top customers (E/F/G 36/29/20% of FY25 [8]) are a few wearable programs that lap the 2026 launch; growth slows to the wearables market plus content gains. Quarter shares 22.0/24.5/26.2/27.3% (FY27) -> 23.0/24.6/25.8/26.6% (FY29): Q1 is the low quarter in FY24 (15.2 of 76.1 = 20.0%) and FY25 (21.7%) [1,3,8]. Variant: downside -15% (a top customer moves a program to a competitor or in-house; no binding purchase commitments [8]), upside +12%.

Q3 4.8, Q4 5.2 (~13% of revenue, the Q2 2026 share). The company deprioritised Mainland China in 2025 ("geopolitical concerns, subsidized competitors creating a price sensitive environment") and says sales there "will continue to be evaluated if they represent higher-margin opportunities" [6,8]; the H1 2026 rebound is from a low base. FY27 +15%, FY28 +5%, FY29 flat: tariffs/US-China trade dispute and export-control risk (10-K risk factors, Huawei association [8]) and local subsidised MCU competition cap it. Variant: downside -40% (tariff or export-control step), upside +10%.

Q3 4.0, Q4 4.5: Q2 2026 doubled q/q (2.880 vs 1.427 [6]); management: net sales outside personal devices expected to double in 2026 vs 2025 [4], target geographies US, Europe, Asia ex-China [6], RONDS industrial partnership [3], Singapore R&D/licensing programme [4]. FY26 12.8 (+192% on 4.3). FY27 +80%, FY28 +45%, FY29 +35%: edge-AI design wins outside wearables (industrial sensors, medical, smart home) converting from 2026 design-ins; Atomiq NPU SoC (12nm) sampling [3,4]. Not disclosed by end market, so the split is by end-customer HQ (flag). Variant: downside -20% (design wins slip, competition from Nordic, ST, NXP, Renesas, Alif [8]), upside +25%.

Q3 2026 47.6% vs guide 46.5-47.5% [5]: the two GM guides beat the midpoint by +1.7 pt each (Q1 46.2 vs 44.5, Q2 47.2 vs 45.5 [3-5]); taken at +0.6 pt because the Q3 guide already embeds "favorable mix and manufacturing efficiencies" and the 10-Q cites rising wafer, packaging and test costs [6]. Q4 47.8%. FY27 48.2%, FY28 48.75%, FY29 49.1%: +0.4-0.5 pt a year from ASP mix (customers moving to Apollo5/510 and later Atomiq raise ASP [6]; FY25 non-GAAP GM +13.5 pt as China fell 50% -> 9% of sales [3,8]); FY28 is ~+1 pt on the Q4 2026 exit for that mix reason, held below the 50%+ of the MCU incumbents because sole-source TSMC wafer pricing [6] and a few large customers limit pricing. Variant: downside -2 pt (TSMC/packaging cost pass-through, a price-down at a top customer), upside +1.5 pt.

Q3 2026 24.0 vs guide 24-25 [5] ("investments to support product development ... including planned intellectual property investments"); record 2/2 at or below the guide (Q1 18.144 vs 18.0-18.5, Q2 19.374 vs 21.0-22.0 [3-5]) so the low end. Q4 25.0. FY27 105.5 (+22%: R&D for 12nm Atomiq, Singapore R&D programme [4], headcount behind capacity expansion [5]); FY28 120.3 (+14%), FY29 134.7 (+12%): opex grows ~6-8 pt slower than revenue, so the loss narrows but non-GAAP operating breakeven (pre-D&A) is not reached in the set (Q4 2029 ~-2.4). Variant: opex +15% in FY27 instead of +22% (see notes, judgment call).

Company non-GAAP net loss adds back income taxes (Q2 2026 provision 1k, FY25 40k [3,5]); the company has a full valuation allowance on US losses (accumulated deficit 374.0M [6]), so no tax on the non-GAAP loss through FY2029. A profit year would first use NOLs (10-K [8]).

model_inputs.structure_note: Thread quarterly driver set kept as is (drivers us_rev, cn_rev, row_rev, ng_gm, ng_opex; FY2025 base; 20 quarters, 6 actual). The business is loss-making through FY2029 on this build, so earnings multiples carry nothing: the single value leg is EV / NTM sales at the horizon (NTM Nov-2027..Oct-2028 revenue from the build, about 208) at an exit multiple from the k-rule, plus net cash and a moratorium adjustment. No DCF (not a neocloud). Normalised-earnings P/E cross-check (playbook 0.2-0.4) is not usable: no positive EPS in the explicit years; the METHOD FIT loss flag does weaken P/E and EV/EBITDA, which is why EV/sales carries all the weight.

model_inputs.gap_note: Peer median is built on 4 numeric peers; AMBA and CEVA are market-cap / next-fiscal-year revenue (P/S proxies, net cash not deducted, fiscal years not calendarised), so they likely overstate EV/NTM sales by some 5-15% (estimate); with them cut 10% the median is 6.0x and the exit 4.9x (about -3% on the target). Nordic is not in the numeric median (no cited share count/FX on the same basis). Financing: cash 366.8 [6] against annual burn of about 20-30 on the build, so no funding gap; a further follow-on after two in 2026 is possible but below 20% (estimate 10%), not booked. Take-out probability 0 (no cited evidence), SLAB/TXN deal is context only [16].
